plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, ruffled, sweetly scented blooms open in lush pillows of petals. They crowd garden borders in shades of blush, rose and crimson. A single plant can hold dozens of flowers at once.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer, with peak bloom in many temperate gardens from May into early June
plants.location: Temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere, including the northern United States, Europe and northern China
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for well over a thousand years, and a well-tended plant can live and bloom for decades.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, cone-shaped clusters of tiny star-shaped florets fill the air with a rich, nostalgic perfume. Whole hedgerows turn violet and lavender as the blooms open.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring, typically May in cooler temperate regions
plants.location: Gardens and hedgerows across northern Europe, the northeastern United States and southern Canada
plants.funFact: Although lilacs are a classic of cottage gardens, the species is native to the rocky hills of southeastern Europe.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A crimson, fiery flower head, ringed by bright red bracts, rises like a torch from the bushland. It is among Australia's most dramatic wildflowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in Australia, usually September to November, so it is not in bloom on May 15
plants.location: Sydney sandstone region, New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: What looks like one big flower is actually a cluster of hundreds of tiny flowers, which draws honeyeater birds that pollinate it.
